messages.author: 54f369bce6d6a87f
messages.subject: Exporting ggvis plots
parts:
I have a Shiny application that generates multiple ggvis plots. The individual controls for each plot that let you switch between SVG and PNG, and let you download either, work. To export all the images simultaneous (via code), however, requires the vg2png (or vg2svg) program that is part of a Vega installation, and the Shiny app cannot find it. Is there an alternative way to export ggvis plots programmatically or, if not, is there any plan to add vg2png?

Thanks.

messages.author: 54f369bce6d6a87f
messages.subject: Re: Exporting ggvis plots
parts:
Martin,

I'm sorry, it turns out I do not have any working ggvis export examples any more. Export relies on a Javascript library (Vega) that I no longer have installed, following an operating system upgrade. The R portion of the code is rather trivial:

library(ggvis)
mtcars %>% ggvis(x = ~wt) %>% export_png(file = "/tmp/myplot.png")

The bulk of the work is installing Vega (and any other required external libraries, which I've since forgotten). The reason for my original post here is that, at least of when I wrote it, Vega was not installed on shinyapps.io; so export worked in my development copy locally but not in the production copy.

For what it's worth, my current version handles plots as follows (using the ggplot2 and plotly libraries):

Server
---------
p <- ggplot(...)
output$myplot <- p $%>% plotly(...) %>% renderPlotly(...)
ggsave("/tmp/myplot", plot = p)

UI
---
plotlyOutput("myplot", ...)

Paul
